content.title: Cori Close - USA Basketball
content.text: UCLA head coach Cori Close has been on the USA Basketball coaching staff for three gold-medal winning squads. This latest coaching stint marked Close’s fourth USA Basketball coaching assignment and third for an international event. Close was head coach for the USA squad that finished with a perfect 7-0 record at the 2021 FIBA U19 World Cup, marking back-to-back U19 titles for Close and the USA. Following the 2021 gold at the FIBA U19 World Cup, Close was named as a co-recipient of the 2021 USA Basketball Developmental Coach of the Year Award, which she shared with 2021 USA Men's U19 head coach Jamie Dixon. Close also helped the USA to a gold medal as an assistant coach for the USA team that won a gold medal with a 7-0 record at the 2019 FIBA U19 World Cup and the 2018 USA U18 squad that finished with a 6-0 record and the gold medal at the 2018 FIBA Americas U18 Championship, which qualified the U.S. for the 2019 U19s. Prior to that, Close was a court coach at the 2017 USA U23 National Team training camp. Close in 2020-21 completed her 10th season at the helm of the UCLA women’s basketball program, beginning in 2011-12, and has compiled an overall record of 215-110 record (.662 winning percentage) through the 2020-21 season. Close, who posted six 20-win seasons at UCLA, has advanced the Bruins to postseason play seven of the nine seasons in which the NCAA Tournament or WNIT were held, including the past five NCAA Tournaments, where she advanced UCLA as far as the Elite 8 in 2018, three Sweet 16s (2016, 2017 and 2019) and the NCAA second round (2021). In 2015, Close piloted the Bruins to the WNIT championship. The 2019-20 campaign, which was cut short due to the COVID-19 pandemic, saw Close lead her team to a 26-5 record and the Pacific-12 Conference Tournament semifinals. Additionally, the Bruins ranked No. 9 in the final USA Today Coaches Poll and No. 10 in the final Associated Press Poll. In 2018-19, Close directed the Bruins to their fourth straight 20-win season and fourth consecutive NCAA Sweet 16 appearance. UCLA finished 22-13 overall, winning 13 of its last 17 games and finishing fourth in the Pacific-12 Conference. UCLA also had seven top-25 wins, including wins over then-ranked No. 2 Oregon and No. 9 Maryland. The Bruins, who ranked second in the NCAA in offensive rebounds per game (17.3), became one of only eight teams to reach the Sweet 16 four years in a row. Close was named the 2018 United States Marine Corps/WBCA NCAA Division I Region 5 Coach of the Year, her second such honor. She also owns 18 seasons of experience as an NCAA assistant coach at UCLA, Florida State University and her alma mater, UC Santa Barbara. Close began her career as an assistant coach at UCLA in 1993-94 and 1994-95 before returning to her alma mater, UC Santa Barbara, as an assistant from 1995-96 to 2003-04. She then was an assistant coach at Florida State University for seven seasons (2004-05 to 2010-11). As an athlete, Close was a four-year starting point guard at UC Santa Barbara who captained the 1992 and 1993 teams to the second round of the NCAA Tournament. A native of Milpitas, California, she was a 1993 All-Big West first-team selection and the MVP of the 1993 Conference Tournament. Close was the first player in school history to record more than 1,000 points and 500 assists for a career. She averaged a school-record 8.3 assists per game in 1993. On April 30, 2005, Close was inducted into the UC Santa Barbara Athletics Hall of Fame.
